# Neural Implicit SLAM

Also called: NeRF-SLAM, Implicit Neural SLAM, Neural Field SLAM

## Overview
Neural Implicit SLAM is a simultaneous localization and mapping technique that constructs a continuous 3D scene representation using a neural network $F$ mapping spatial coordinates to scene properties, while simultaneously optimizing camera poses $T_t$ [S1, S3]. It differs from explicit grid-based SLAM (e.g., [Dense Grid SLAM](12345-dense-grid-slam.md)) by offering resolution-independent geometry and from traditional feature-based SLAM (e.g., [ORB-SLAM](12340-orb-slam.md)) by leveraging dense photometric and geometric constraints for tracking [S3]. Unlike [Gaussian Splatting SLAM](12350-gaussian-splatting-slam.md), which uses explicit parametric primitives, this family relies on implicit neural fields, allowing for smoother [surface representations](#22781-surface-representation.md) and easier integration of semantic information, though often at higher computational cost during initialization [S1].

## Shared principles
The family relies on a neural network $F$ that maps spatial coordinates $\mathbf{x}$ to scene properties [G]. For appearance, $F$ outputs color $\mathbf{c}$ and volume density $\sigma$ (or occupancy) [S1]. For geometry, $F$ may output a Signed Distance Function ([SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)) value [S1]. Rendering is performed via volume rendering or [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md): points are sampled along camera rays, properties are predicted by $F$, and results are aggregated using alpha [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) or weighted sums [S1]. Optimization jointly updates the network weights and camera poses $T_t$ to minimize photometric ($\ell_{rgb}$) and geometric ($\ell_{depth}$ or SDF) losses [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Hybrid Implicit Neural Representation SLAM Sampling & Optimization](23458-hybrid-implicit-neural-representation-slam-sampling-optimiza.md)
This method implements a real-time RGB-D SLAM framework that optimizes an [implicit neural representation](#19545-implicit-neural-representation-inr.md) using hybrid spatial encodings (combining dense or [hash grids](#936-hash-grids.md) with tri-planes) and a [composite loss](#15617-composite-loss.md) function tailored for tracking and mapping. It solves the problem of efficient, high-accuracy scene reconstruction and pose estimation by jointly optimizing the neural implicit function and camera poses using cached sampled rays. Unlike pure neural [implicit methods](#12421-implicit-methods-sdf-based.md) which may suffer from high memory usage or slow convergence, this approach uses explicit hybrid encoding to accelerate feature lookup while maintaining the continuous representation benefits of neural fields. See [Hybrid Implicit Neural Representation SLAM Sampling & Optimization](23458-hybrid-implicit-neural-representation-slam-sampling-optimiza.md) for implementation details.

### SLAIM
SLAIM is a SLAM method that introduces a coarse-to-fine tracking pipeline and improves photometric [bundle adjustment](#8540-bundle-adjustment.md) for NeRF-based mapping [S1]. It maintains [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)’s original volume density formulation while introducing a KL regularization over the ray termination distribution [S1]. This addresses the challenge of high-frequency renderings in NeRF hindering image alignment [S1].

### SNI-SLAM
SNI-SLAM is a dense NeRF-based RGB-D SLAM system for accurate real-time 3D semantic mapping [S1]. It introduces a hierarchical semantic encoding and cross-attention mechanism to enable mutual reinforcement between appearance, geometry, and semantics modalities [S1]. It further proposes a novel one-way decoder design to enhance inter-modal information flow without reverse interference [S1].

### KN-SLAM
KN-SLAM is a NeRF-based SLAM method that integrates local feature correspondences for [coarse pose initialization](#19708-silhouette-based-camera-to-object-registration.md) and joint optimization [S1]. It uses global image features and local matches for explicit loop detection [S1]. It performs pose graph optimization and global refinement of the neural map to ensure consistency [S1].

### VI-NeRF-SLAM
VI-NeRF-SLAM merges traditional SLAM method benefits with NeRF mapping to facilitate immediate, dense 3D scene reconstruction online without prior training [S2]. It estimates pixel depth and pose based on constraints in reprojecting feature points [S2]. It refines the depiction of 3D scenes through the use of [ray integration](#18634-ray-integration.md) and networks [S2]. It includes a dynamic error correction technique for IMUs [S2]. It includes a method for managing closed loops in NeRF mapping [S2]. It surpasses current benchmark techniques in reconstruction and tracking precision on Euroc and Replica datasets, particularly in scenarios limited to grayscale imagery [S2].

### NeRF-SLAM Problem Formulation
NeRF-SLAM Problem Formulation defines the task as a continuous online learning problem where a stream of synchronized RGB-D input frames is processed to optimize a neural implicit function $F$ and camera pose $T_t$ using cached sampled rays [S3]. For each pixel $\mathbf{x}$ in an RGB-D frame, $N$ points are sampled along the camera ray, each at distance $d_i$ with position $\mathbf{p}_i$ [S3]. Appearance $\mathbf{c}_i$ and geometric properties $g_i$ are predicted for each sample point $\mathbf{p}_i$ using the learnable neural implicit function $F$ [S3]:
$$ (\mathbf{c}_i, g_i) = F(\mathbf{p}_i) $$
The weight $w_i$ for each sample is determined by a geometric rendering function $G$ applied to the geometric properties:
$$ w_i = G(g_i) $$
Rendered color and depth are computed as weighted sums:
$$ \tilde{\mathbf{c}}_{\mathbf{x}} = \sum_{i=1}^N w_i \cdot \mathbf{c}_i, \quad \tilde{d}_{\mathbf{x}} = \sum_{i=1}^N w_i \cdot d_i $$
Optimization minimizes photometric and geometric constraints: $e^p_{\mathbf{x}} = \tilde{\mathbf{c}}_{\mathbf{x}} - \mathbf{c}_{\mathbf{x}}$ and $e^g_{\mathbf{x}} = \tilde{d}_{\mathbf{x}} - d_{\mathbf{x}}$ [S3]. The weight is formulated as $w_i = G(F_{geo}(\mathbf{p}_i))$, where $F \in \mathcal{F}$ and $G \in \mathcal{G}$ [S3].

### SE3
[SE3](#11475-rigid-body-transformation-se3.md) is a method that addresses loop closure correction for implicit maps by implementing an equivariant mapping from SE3 to feature space, synchronously adjusting camera poses and implicit map representations [S4]. It leverages the frontend localization module of ORB-SLAM2 and uses a voxel grid as the backend to construct a SLAM system that achieves loop closure correction for implicit maps [S4].

## Background
Neural Implicit SLAM emerged from the integration of [Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) (NeRF) [S1] with traditional SLAM pipelines. Early works focused on offline reconstruction, but real-time RGB-D SLAM variants like the one described in [S1] introduced hybrid encodings (hash grids/tri-planes) to accelerate training. The problem formulation as a continuous online learning task with cached rays was formalized in [S3]. Variants like SLAIM [S1] and SNI-SLAM [S1] addressed specific issues like high-frequency rendering artifacts and semantic consistency. VI-NeRF-SLAM [S2] extended this to monocular/IMU scenarios with dynamic error correction. SE3 [S4] tackled the irreversibility of implicit maps for loop closure. The family is widely used in robotics for dense 3D mapping where explicit geometry is difficult to maintain [S1, S3].
